title: 1965 AHSME Problem 12
statement: A rhombus is inscribed in triangle \(ABC\) in such a way that one of its vertices is \(A\) and two of its sides lie along \(AB\) and \(AC.\) If \(AC=6\) inches, \(AB=12\) inches, and \(BC=8\) inches, the side of the rhombus, in inches, is:

solutions.text:
Use \(A\) as the origin and let the vectors to \(B,C\) be \(u,v.\) If the rhombus side is \(s,\) its opposite vertex is \((\frac{s}{12})u+(\frac{s}{6})v.\) A point lies on \(BC\) when these coefficients sum to \(1.\) Thus \[ \frac{s}{12}+\frac{s}{6}=1,\] giving \(s=4.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the rhombus side be \(s\), with adjacent vertices \(\frac{s}{12}\) of the way along \(AB\) and \(\frac{s}{6}\) along \(AC\)
The opposite rhombus vertex lies on \(BC\), so its two affine coefficients sum to \(1\)
